messages:
elaine: Heads up — after yesterday's RBAC refactor the operator-role binding isn't reconciling on Dedicated clusters behind the VPC allowlist. Getting 403s for the `redwood-operator` when tenant-init runs.
mike: saw this in staging-dedicated-west this morning. pod logs show: `forbidden: user \"system:serviceaccount:redwood-system:operator\" cannot create rolebindings.rbac.authorization.k8s.io`.
jmorris: can you paste `kubectl get rolebinding -n redwood-system` output? curious if subjects changed in the refactor.
elaine: here —
```
NAME                     ROLE                 AGE
redwood-operator binding  ClusterRole/admin    18h
subjects: 
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: operator
    namespace: redwood-system
```
sec-bot: [alert] RoleBindingMismatch detected for cluster dedicated-west at 2026-03-20T09:12Z — expected subjects differ from live state
sarah: my first guess is the VPC allowlist mutating webhook or ingress proxy is stripping/rewriting source headers so the webhook policy denies RBAC changes coming from control plane IPs. operator calls originate from control-plane private IPs, which might not be in the allowlist.
ops: checked the webhook config — it relies on `X-Forwarded-For` to map requests to cluster IPs. in Private control plane we don't inject that header for operator requests, so the webhook treats them as external and denies the write. quick patch: set proxy to forward `X-Forwarded-For` for internal requests.
jmorris: if we flip the proxy behavior, we need an audit trail. propose temporary policy exception for dedicated clusters so operator can reconcile, and then lock down after patch and validate with audit logs.
elaine: i'll add an exception to `rbac-exempt` for dedicated-west and watch the operator reconcile. rolling now.
ops: patch deployed, exception added to dedicated-west. operator reconciled and tenant-init jobs moved from CrashLoopBackOff to Completed. noticed while looking that one tenant pod was missing the KMS annotation (separate issue) — logged as #INC-472.
sarah: OK — this is a moderate risk: if webhook/proxy misconfig allows operator RBAC changes during exception window we need a short incident note and a follow-up hardening task. @jmorris can you capture attack surface and mitigation steps?
jmorris: will do. plan: 1) collect audit logs for the window, 2) add unit/integration test for webhook header handling, 3) CI gate that ensures dedicated clusters have correct proxy settings before rollout. will create PRs and a short postmortem doc.
elaine: thanks — proceeding to deploy same exception to dedicated-east after jmorris' tests are in. will update here when done. :thumbsup:
